members.claim: The tool-call IDs on the preserved latest assistant turn are never added to the `used` set. `resolve()` can therefore turn an older ID into one that already exists unchanged in the latest turn. Example: an older `call_1` becomes `call1` while the latest turn already uses `call1`, or under strict9 a truncated or hashed ID collides with a preserved ID. The transcript then has duplicate tool IDs, results pair with the wrong call, and the provider can reject the request. Before mapping, add the preserved IDs to `used`, and map each one to itself.

members.claim: Reserve preserved tool-call IDs before sanitizing history
members.evidence: When a historical ID sanitizes to an ID in the preserved latest turn (for example, historical `a_b` and latest `ab`), the historical call is rewritten to `ab` while the latest call remains `ab`. Because preserved IDs are never added to `used`, this introduces duplicate tool-call IDs and ambiguous result pairing, defeating the existing transcript-wide collision protection. Reserve the preserved IDs before resolving historical IDs so historical calls receive a unique alternative.
